identificationModule.briefTitle: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effect of MIN-102 on the Progression of Friedreich's Ataxia in Male and Female Patients
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Double-Blind, Placebo-controlled Study on the Effects of MIN-102 on Biochemical, Imaging, Neurophysiological, and Clinical Markers in Patients With Friedreich's Ataxia

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study on the effects of MIN-102 on Biochemical, Imaging, neurophysiological, and clinical markers in patients with Friedreich's Ataxia
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
This study investigated whether treatment with MIN-102 was able to influence clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging parameters, as well as various peripheral and central nervous system biochemical markers related to mitochondrial dysfunction, in patients with Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA), over a period of 48 weeks in a double-blind, placebo-controlled design.

Patients were screened following written consent (and assent if the patient was a minor) at the Screening visit (V-1). Eligible patients attended a Baseline visit (V0) within a maximum of 28 days after V-1 and were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive an individualized starting dose of MIN-102 or placebo, which they took daily for 48 weeks. Patients received individualized starting doses based on gender and age, which were subsequently modified based on pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters obtained from blood samples at V1 to achieve a target MIN-102 exposure of 170 μg.hr/mL.

In addition to the Screening visit (V-1) and Baseline visit (V0), patients were evaluated at 2 interim safety visits (ISV) occurring 2 and 8 weeks after V0 (ISV1 and ISV2; permitted to be home visits performed by a Good Clinical Practice \[GCP\]-certified nurse), and at 4 weeks (V1), 12 weeks (V2), 24 weeks (V3), 36 weeks (V4), and 48 weeks (V5) after V0.

Results of all scheduled assessments were made available to the investigator as soon as possible. Patients received regularly scheduled phone calls at 6, 10, 16, 20, 28, 32, 40, and 44 weeks after V0 to review changes in concomitant medications and adverse events (AEs), particularly for symptoms possibly indicative of cardiac failure. A Final Follow-up Visit (FUV) took place 4 weeks after the last dose of study drug.

Evaluations consisted of imaging evaluations at V0, V3, and V5, evaluations of clinical status using the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), cerebellar composite functional scale (CCFS), global clinical rating scales, and patient questionnaires at V0, V3, and V5, assessment of biochemical markers in plasma at V0, V2, V3, and V5, and blood sampling for plasma levels of MIN-102 and its main metabolite (M3) at all scheduled on-site visits (except for ISV1 and ISV2). Assessments for safety and tolerability included collection of AEs, as well as electrocardiograms (ECGs), echocardiograms, and laboratory tests. Palatability was assessed at V0, V1, V2, V3, and V4. Measurements of motor evoked potentials (MEPs) and assessment of biochemical markers in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were optional evaluations at V0, V3, and V5. All assessments for safety, tolerability, and biochemical markers in plasma were also performed at premature discontinuation.

armGroups.label: MIN-102
armGroups.description: MIN-102 (5-\[\[4-\[2-\[5-(1-Hydroxyethyl)-2-pyridinyl\]ethoxy\]phenyl\]methyl\]-2,4-thiazolidinedione hydrochloride (1:1)). Dosing is once daily at approximately the same time each morning throughout the entire treatment phase (48 weeks).

armGroups.label: Placebo
armGroups.description: Matches MIN-102 visually and by taste. Dosing is once daily at approximately the same time each morning throughout the entire treatment phase (48 weeks).

interventions.name: MIN-102
interventions.description: Once-daily dosing with a volume specified by the pharmacokinetic specialist to achieve the desired plasma exposure. MIN-102 oral suspension, strength 15 mg/ml.

interventions.name: Placebo
interventions.description: Once-daily dosing with a volume specified by the pharmacokinetic specialist. Oral suspension.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in spinal cord area cervical segment C2-C3 [mm²]
primaryOutcomes.description: Spinal cord area cervical segment C2-C3 area was assessed at Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48 by morphometric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measurements. Morphometric changes in MRI parameters are associated with measures of clinical decline. In normal disease etiology, the spinal cord exhibits an initial decrease in area, and then reaches a plateau after 7-8 years from disease onset.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in SARA total score at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: The SARA is an 8-item clinical rating scale. Five of the items are scored with points between 0 and 4, gait is scored with points between 0 and 8, and stance and speech disturbance are scored with points between 0 and 6. Total maximum score is 40 indicating maximum disability. SARA was determined at Screening, Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in cervical spinal cord (C2-C7) in fractional anisotropy at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: MRI diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) was used for assessments at Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48 to measure rate of disease progression.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in cervical spinal cord (C2-C7) in mean, axial, and radial diffusivity (10-³ mm²/s) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: MRI DTI was used for assessments at Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48 to measure rate of disease progression.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in spinal cord total N-acetylaspartate concentration/myo-inositol (tNAA/mIns) ratio as assessed by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: This metabolite ratio was used to measure rate of disease progression at Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) for iron concentration (ppb) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: QSM was acquired in the cerebellum, using a gradient echo MRI sequence. It was used to quantify local tissue properties of the dentate nucleus, which reflect iron concentration. Measurements were taken at Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in dentate nuclei volume at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: QSM was acquired in the cerebellum, using a gradient echo MRI sequence. It was used to quantify local tissue properties of the dentate nucleus, including estimating the volume of the dentate nucleus. Reported values were normalized by total intracranial volume (TICV) and were dimensionless. Measurements were taken at Baseline, Week 24, and Week 48.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in fixel-based analysis (FBA) of the brain at Week 48: fiber density (FD)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Diffusion metrics related to the integrity of the corticospinal tract (CST), selected brain regions, and spinal cord fibers were extracted from diffusion-weighted images. Fixel-based analyses of the CST, the superior and inferior cerebellar peduncles (SCP and ICP), the posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC), the superior corna radiata (SCR), and the medial lemniscus (mLEM) were summarized to determine changes to the fibers. Fiber density measured number of axons in these structures.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in fixel-based analysis (FBA) of the brain at Week 48: fiber cross-section (FC)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Diffusion metrics related to the integrity of the CST, selected brain regions, and spinal cord fibers were extracted from diffusion-weighted images. Fixel-based analyses of the CST, the SCP and ICP, the PLIC, the SCR, and the mLEM were summarized to determine changes to the fibers. Fiber cross-section measured the area of the fiber cross-section in these structures.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in fixel-based analysis (FBA) of the brain at Week 48: fiber density and cross-section (FDC)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Diffusion metrics related to the integrity of the CST, selected brain regions, and spinal cord fibers were extracted from diffusion-weighted images. Fixel-based analyses of the CST, the SCP and ICP, the PLIC, the SCR, and the mLEM were summarized to determine changes to the fibers. Fiber density and cross-section was a combination of both FD and FC in these structures.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in Cerebellar Composite Functional Scale (CCFS) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: The CCFS is a derived score based on results of two tests which are carried out with the dominant hand: the 9-hole peg test and clicking. The 9-hole peg test measures the time it takes for the patient to place 9 pegs in holes. In the clicking test, the subject has to press 2 buttons with the index finger of their dominant hand. The buttons are mounted on a board and have to be pressed in an alternating fashion for 10 times. As an outcome, Z-scores were calculated by subtracting the expected time that was obtained from healthy controls from the time measured in the patient. CCFS was calculated as log10 (7+Z pegboard dominant hand/10 + 4\*Z click dominant hand/10). The CCFS assesses the severity of cerebellar ataxia; higher scores indicate greater severity of disease.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in quality of life as measured by European Quality of Life 5 Dimensions (EQ-5D-5L) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: The EQ-5D-5L is a patient-rated scale with 5 dimensions (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression) where patients are asked to rate themselves according to presented responses at 5 levels of severity for each dimension (level 1 indicates no problems; level 5 indicates disability). They also rate their overall health on the particular study day on a scale from 0 to 100 points, with 0 indicating the worst possible health. The outcomes are the sum of the scores of the responses on the 5 dimensions, the overall rating of health in terms of points, and an index score based on both scores. Index scores range between 0 and 1 (with higher scores indicating better quality of life).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in fatigue severity scale (FSS) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: Patients rate their level of fatigue on the FSS by responding to 9 presented statements where a score of 1 means maximum disagreement and 7 means strongest agreement. The outcome is the sum of scores over the 9 items. Higher scores indicate greater severity of fatigue.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in Activities of Daily Living subscale of Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale (FARS) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: Activities of daily living were assessed by patients using section II of the FARS. Section II contained 9 items where subjects were rated on a scale between 0 (normal function) and 4 (most severely disturbed function). The scores for the individual 9 items are added to yield the total score. A higher score indicates a greater level of disability.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change from Baseline in Clinician Global Impression of Severity (CGI-S) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: The CGI-S rates the severity of illness based on a 1-7 point scale completed by the investigator, where 1 = "normal, not at all ill" and 7 = "among the most extremely-ill patients".

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Assessment from Baseline in Clinician Global Impression of Improvement (CGI-I) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: The CGI-I is a tool for assessing total overall improvement as judged by the investigator that considers whether or not the improvement is entirely due to the study medication treatment. The CGI-I rates the improvement based on a 1-7 point scale, where 1 = "very much improved" and 7 = "very much worse".

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Assessment from Baseline in Patient Global Impression of Improvement (PGI-I) at Week 48
secondaryOutcomes.description: The PGI-I is a tool for assessing total overall improvement as judged by the patient during study medication treatment. The PGI-I rates the improvement based on a 1-7 point scale, where 1 = "very much improved" and 7 = "very much worse".

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Percentage of patients responding to palatability of study drug questions
secondaryOutcomes.description: Palatability of the study drug was assessed by the patient at Baseline, Week 4, Week 12, Week 24, and Week 36 immediately after swallowing and 10 minutes after swallowing. Patients rated the taste as "Super-good", "Good", "Neutral", "Bad", and "Super-bad". Patients were also asked if they would take the study drug every day (possible responses were "Yes", "Not sure", and "No". The percentage of patients in each category was presented.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline, Week 4, Week 12, Week 24, and Week 36

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Frequency and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Adverse events were monitored from Baseline until the Final Follow-up Visit (28 days after the last dose of study drug). TEAEs were defined as AEs occurring on or after the first dose of study drug. Number of patients with AEs and SAEs graded between Grade 1 (mild) and Grade 5 (death) was presented.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 52 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Vital signs: percentage change from Baseline in body weight (kg)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Weight measured at Baseline and all subsequent in-person visits.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 52 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Vital signs: change from Baseline in blood pressure (mmHg)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure measured at Baseline and all subsequent in-person visits.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 52 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Vital signs: change from Baseline in pulse rate (beats/min)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Measured at Baseline and all subsequent in-person visits.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 52 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Vital signs: change from Baseline in body temperature (°C)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Measured at baseline and all subsequent in-person visits.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 52 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of patients with abnormal, clinically significant electrocardiogram (ECG) and echocardiogram interpretations
secondaryOutcomes.description: Echocardiograms were performed at Screening, Week 4, Week 12, Week 24, Week 24, Week 48, and the Final Follow-up Visit; 12-lead ECGs were performed at Screening, Baseline (pre-dose and 3 hours post-dose), 3 hours post-dose at Week 4, Week 12, Week 24, Week 36, and at Week 48 and the Final Follow-up Visit. The number of patients with normal, abnormal not clinically significant, abnormal clinically significant, and not assessable was tabulated.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 52 weeks)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of patients with abnormal, clinically significant physical examination findings
secondaryOutcomes.description: Body systems examined included abdomen, extremities, heart, lungs, and skin.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Screening to Final Follow-up Visit (approximately 56 weeks)

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male and female subjects aged ≥12 and ≤60 years, inclusive, with a genetically confirmed diagnosis of Friedreich's Ataxia.
* Be able to walk \>10 meters with support (two special sticks, stroller, or accompanying person).
* Total score on the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) of \<25.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age of onset of disease ≥25 years.
* Higher degree of cardiomyopathy assessed by echocardiogram.
* Diabetes.

identificationModule.briefTitle: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of MIN-102 (IMP) in Male AMN Patients
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multinational, Multicenter Study With Open-label Treatment Extension to Assess the Effect of MIN-102 on the Progression of Adrenomyeloneuropathy in Male Patients With X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a Phase II/III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, two parallel-group study in male patients with the adrenomyeloneuropathy (AMN) phenotype of X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD) to assess the efficacy and safety of MIN-102 treatment. Study sites will consist of specialist referral centers experienced in the management of adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD).
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
In Part 1 of the study, eligible patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive leriglitazone or placebo. For patients randomized to leriglitazone, dosing was adjusted on an individual-patient basis to achieve the target plasma leriglitazone exposure, with a maximum allowed range of ±20%. Patients randomized to placebo received the same amount of a matched placebo suspension. Blood samples to determine leriglitazone plasma concentrations were obtained at all visits after the baseline visit (V0). Dose-adjustment recommendations were made by a pharmacokinetic (PK) expert from the central laboratory who was unblinded to PK data. For patients not tolerating the target plasma exposure, the investigator could reduce the study medication dose at any timepoint by up to 50%. To preserve the blind, random dose adjustments were made for the patients receiving placebo.

Part 2 was an open-label treatment extension study which started immediately after the day of last treatment in Part 1 at V6, which, after 96 weeks of double-blind treatment in Part 1, was simultaneously the baseline visit of Part 2 of the study. All patients in Part 2 (including those randomized to placebo in Part 1) received a leriglitazone dose to achieve the predefined target plasma exposure. All patients who were taking doses of ≤ the starting dose in Part 1 at the end of Part 1 (V6) started Part 2 with the same dose. All other patients reverted to the Part 1 starting dose of leriglitazone oral suspension. Patients and investigators were advised that dose adjustments could occur in both groups, those previously assigned to leriglitazone and to placebo, since patients who were on a stable leriglitazone dose during Part 1 may no longer have been at their optimum exposure level at Week 96.

After the potential adjustment informed by PK results obtained at 100 weeks (V7) and 108 weeks (V8), the study medication dosage could not otherwise be changed except if required for safety/tolerability reasons. Downwards adjustments of the dose in this case could be introduced, but the minimum exposure had to be achieved. Patients who experienced study medication-related AEs and who could not tolerate the study medication, even at the minimum permitted exposure level, were discontinued from the study.

In Part 2 patients were evaluated with 144 weeks of daily administration of study medication and periodic on-site visits and follow-up phone calls. After 144 weeks of daily administration in Part 2, regular visits and safety visits or follow-up phone calls were to each take place at 6-month intervals for an unlimited time until either: (1) the patient withdrew consent; (2) significant safety or tolerability issues appeared and/or the patient's general health status, in the clinical judgment of the investigator, declined to an extent that the risks of treatment with leriglitazone outweighed the potential benefits; (3) the patient underwent hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation; (4) leriglitazone received marketing authorization for the treatment of AMN; or (5) Minoryx Therapeutics decided to terminate this study, whichever of these events occurred first.

interventions.name: Leriglitazone
interventions.description: Administered once daily in the morning. Dosing was adjusted on an individual-patient basis to achieve target plasma leriglitazone exposure, with a maximum allowed range of ±20%.

interventions.name: Placebo

primaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the total distance walked (meters) in the 6-minute walk test

Part 2: Long-term safety and tolerability of leriglitazone, assessed in terms of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), vital signs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), and clinical laboratory tests
primaryOutcomes.description: The number of patients with AEs, SAEs, and SUSARs, and with abnormal vital signs (body weight, blood pressure, pulse rate), 12-lead ECGs (heart rate, PR interval, RR interval, QRS duration, QT interval, QTc interval \[Bazzett's and Fridericia's\] and investigator interpretation of the ECG profile), and clinical laboratory tests (hematology, blood chemistry including parameters for adrenal function, urinalysis and sample for cytology) will be presented.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through study completion, up to 335 weeks

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in body sway amplitude - total (eyes closed/feet apart)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Total body sway was measured (mm) using a portable plantar pressure system. Change from baseline in total body sway amplitude under the eyes closed/feet apart condition is presented.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Percentage of patients reporting an improvement from baseline in the Patient Global Impression - Improvement scale (PGI-I) at Week 96
secondaryOutcomes.description: The PGI-I is a tool for assessing improvement as judged by the patient. It is a 1-7 point weighted scale, ranging from "very much improved" (1) to "very much worse" (7).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in Severity Score System for Progressive Myelopathy (SSPROM)
secondaryOutcomes.description: The SSPROM is a scale covering 5 domains (patient-reported motor disability, examined motor disability, spasticity and hyperreflexia, sensory loss, and patient information on sphincter dysfunction), ranging from 0 (total disability) to 100 (normal).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the overall score of the Qualiveen Short Form Quality of Life Questionnaire for Urinary Disorders (Qualiveen-SF)
secondaryOutcomes.description: The Qualiveen-SF overall score ranges from 0 (not at all affected by the problem) to 4 (extremely affected by the problem).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Changes from baseline to Week 96 in body sway amplitude
secondaryOutcomes.description:
Body sway was measured (mm) using a portable plantar pressure system, considering total sway, antero-posterior (A-P) sway, and mediolateral (M-L) sway. Body sway was measured under 4 conditions: eyes closed/feet apart; eyes closed/feet together; eyes open/feet apart; eyes open/feet together.

Changes from baseline in total body sway amplitude (eyes closed/feet together; eyes open/feet apart; eyes open/feet together), sway average amplitude A-P (all 4 conditions), and sway average amplitude M-L (all 4 conditions) are presented.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) - ambulation score
secondaryOutcomes.description: The Kurtzke EDSS is a widely utilized method of quantifying disability and monitoring changes in the level of disability over time. It is based on a standard neurological examination. The ambulation score within EDSS ranges from 0 (unrestricted) to 12 (essentially restricted to bed or chair or perambulated in wheelchair).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Percentage of patients for whom an improvement from baseline was reported in the Clinical Global Impression - Improvement scale (CGI-I) at Week 96
secondaryOutcomes.description: The CGI-I is a tool for assessing total overall improvement as judged by the investigator that considers whether or not the improvement is entirely due to the study medication treatment. It is a 1-7 point weighted scale, ranging from "very much improved" (1) to "very much worse" (7).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the European Quality of Life 5 Dimension 5 Level (EQ-5D-5L) index
secondaryOutcomes.description: The EQ-5D-5L consists of 5 individual domains: mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression along with a health scale. The index value (health scale), which ranges from 0 to 1 (higher scores represent better health) was used for the evaluation of this outcome measure secondary endpoint.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Percentage of patients for whom a worsening from baseline was reported in the Clinical Global Impression - Severity of Illness scale (CGI-S) at Week 96
secondaryOutcomes.description: The CGI-S is a rating for severity of illness based on a 1-7 point weighted scale that is filled in by the investigator at the start of treatment. It assesses "normal, not at all ill" (1) to "among the most extremely ill patients" (7).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the dynamometry maximum value (kg) of the leg with the lowest average value at baseline
secondaryOutcomes.description: Dynamometry was performed using a hand-held device that was used to measure hip flexion strength in both legs. Measurements were repeated 3 times over the course of 5 minutes. The maximum value out of the 3 measurements of the leg with the lowest average value (kg) at baseline was used for analysis.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the percentage out of 60 points of the Multiple Sclerosis Walking Scale, 12-item (MSWS-12)
secondaryOutcomes.description: The MSWS-12 is combined into a single score by summing the score for each of the 12 questions (maximum score of 60) and calculating a percentage, where a higher percentage means a greater impact on walking ability.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in the total score of the International Index of Erectile Function questionnaire (IIEF)
secondaryOutcomes.description: The IIEF was combined into a single score by creating 5 domains and summing the individual domain scores. The IIEF total score ranges from 0 (negative) to 75 (positive).

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Progression of cerebral lesions in cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
secondaryOutcomes.description:
The progression of cerebral lesions in MRI was assessed by central readers blinded to treatment. Progression was defined as:

* Occurrence of inflammatory (gadolinium \[Gd\]-positive) lesions, or
* Growth of existing noninflammatory lesions since screening or baseline, or
* Occurrence of new noninflammatory lesions after screening or baseline

The number of patients with cerebral lesions present at baseline, and the number of patients showing progression of cerebral lesions at Weeks 48 and 96 is presented.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Change from baseline to Week 96 in Loes severity scores on the MRI
secondaryOutcomes.description: Loes severity score was assessed by central readers using standardized rating with severity scores for 9 brain regions and atrophy. Loes scores range from 0 (normal) to 34 (most severe). Note that increases in Loes severity score are expected in patients who showed cerebral progression.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 2: Progression of cerebral lesions in cerebral MRI
secondaryOutcomes.description:
The progression of cerebral lesions in MRI was assessed by central readers blinded to treatment. Progression was defined as:

* Number of patients with progression between Week 144 and Week 192, and between Week 192 and Week 240
* Number of patients with progression per year

secondaryOutcomes.description: Loes severity score was assessed by central readers using standardized rating with severity scores for 9 brain regions and atrophy. Loes scores range from 0 (normal) to 34 (most severe). Note that increases in Loes severity score are expected in patients who showed cerebral progression.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Part 2: The number of SAE reports on diagnosis of clinically progressive cALD as judged by the investigator taking into account both MRI results and an overall clinical evaluation

The following are presented:

Number of patients who entered Part 2 and did not develop progressive cALD in Part 1

* Number of patients diagnosed with clinically progressive cALD between Week 144 and Week 192, and between Week 192 and Week 240
* Number of patients diagnosed with clinically progressive cALD per year

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria for Part 1 of the study:

* Male and between 18-65 years of age.
* Diagnosed with X-ALD based on genetic testing.
* Clinical evidence of spinal cord involvement.

Additional Inclusion Criteria for Part 2 of the study:

\- Completion of the entire 96-week double-blind period of the study (Part 1).

Exclusion Criteria for both parts of the study:

* Any other chronic neurological disease with signs of spastic paraplegia, such as hereditary spastic paraplegia, multiple sclerosis, etc.
* Presence of inflammatory (Gd-enhancing) MRI lesions or any abnormality other than those mentioned in the inclusion criteria.
* Known type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
* Known intolerance to pioglitazone or any other thiazolidinedione.
* Taking or have taken honokiol, pioglitazone or other thiazolidinediones within the 6 months prior to screening.
* Previous bone marrow transplantation.
* Previous or current history of cancer (other than treated basal cell carcinoma).
* Previous or current history of congestive heart failure.

interventions.name: MIN-102
interventions.description: Once-daily dosing with a volume specified by the pharmacokineteic specialist to achive the desired plasma exposure. Min-102 Oral suspension, strength 15mg/ml.

primaryOutcomes.measure: evaluate whether MIN-102 can halt disease progression of cALD if administered prior to hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT), as determined by serial clinical and MRI investigations in pediatric subjects.
"arrested disease" will be assessed at 24 weeks and at 96 weeks
primaryOutcomes.description: arrested disease is defined using: Cahnge in NFS from Baseline, Free of MFD and lack of lesion progression on MRI

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Males aged ≥2 and ≤12 years with a diagnosis of X-linked ALD
* White matter involvement as determined by cerebral MRI lesions without Gd enhancement at baseline (Population 1), or with Gd enhancement at baseline (Population 2).
* Major Functional Disabilities (MFD) score of 0.
* Baseline Loes score \>0 and ≤10
* Gadolinium Intensity Score \>2

Exclusion Criteria:

* Previous HSCT
* Too far progressed inflammatory brain lesions
